shared: [untitled BTM module] Granulocyte development and activation is the theme here: a transcriptional core that commits myeloid progenitors to the neutrophil lineage, a cytokine receptor that drives their expansion, and signalling and cytoskeletal components that let mature cells respond. PU.1 and the retinoic acid receptor set and maintain myeloid identity, which is why blockade of retinoid signalling in promyelocytic leukaemia arrests cells short of maturity and why pharmacological retinoid treatment restores it.
response to granulocyte macrophage colony-stimulating factor
additional: [untitled BTM module] This grouping describes the transcriptional programme of immature myeloid progenitors in the bone marrow, the stage at which granulocyte, mast cell and erythroid potential is still being resolved and primary granule proteins are first made. Its hallmark products are the azurophilic granule enzymes myeloperoxidase and neutrophil elastase, together with the mast cell protease carboxypeptidase A3 and the promyelocyte membrane marker MS4A3, so the signature marks promyelocytes and their close relatives rather than mature blood cells.

additional: [untitled BTM module] The grouping is anchored on post-transcriptional and transcriptional control of gene expression in neural and developing tissues. Three sequence-specific RNA-binding proteins carry much of its identity: the neuronal ELAV-family protein ELAVL3 and the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element binding protein CPEB3 govern stability, localisation and translation of mRNAs in neurons, where CPEB3 acts on transcripts encoding glutamate receptor subunits and contributes to synaptic plasticity and memory, while YBX1 is a broadly acting mRNA packaging and translational regulator.
